1: ---
2: name: hyperframes
3: description: HyperFrames render contract, Studio editing and references. Open for every video edit.
4: ---
5: 
6: # HyperFrames
7: 
8: HTML becomes video by seeking a paused timeline: identical renders, editable in Studio.
9: 
10: `index.html` is the root: it declares variables and mounts one scene per `compositions/` file. A website subject: hf_capture_website when offered, else `hyperframes capture <url> -o "$(mktemp -d)/site" --json`; read its output.
11: Render only when asked for a file (export, render, download, copies), never in the cloud unless asked: start it yourself with hf_render_video when offered (over MCP render.start, render.wait), count for N identical files; never tell them to click Export.
12: 
13: Build what was asked: no voiceover, captions or new aspect ratio unless asked or in the source; a film over ~15 s that tells something gets music and sound on visible actions unless they asked for silence (`media-use`). New video: 1920×1080, 30 fps. Before hand-writing an effect, transition, caption style, chart or card, search the registry (`hyperframes-registry`).
14: 
15: ## Contract
16: 
17: `hyperframes check --json` reports most violations with a `Fix:` line.
18: 
19: 1. Every timed element has `class="clip"`, `data-start` and `data-duration` in seconds, and shows over `[start, start + duration)`: land an end state just before its end. `data-track-index` is a lane, not paint order (`z-index`): a new clip takes the lowest one free over its time.
20: 2. The video's length is the root's `data-duration`: overrun is cut, an early end holds the last frame.
21: 3. Each composition builds one paused timeline and registers it after its tweens: `window.__timelines["<data-composition-id>"] = tl`.
22: 4. No `Date.now()`, unseeded `Math.random()`, network fetches, timers or `repeat: -1`. All visuals are a function of timeline time.
23: 5. Never tween `display`, `visibility` or `autoAlpha` on a `.clip`; animate a child.
24: 6. No CSS `transform` on an element GSAP transforms; animate transforms, not `left`/`top`/`width`/`height`.
25: 7. Never `play()`, `pause()` or seek media. A `<video>` with sound keeps it (`data-has-audio="true"`); silent footage is `muted`. Separate `<audio>` is for music, voiceover, replacement sound or a J/L cut.
26: 8. Every `<audio>` has an `id` or it is left out of the mix. No `crossorigin` on media.
27: 9. Time a `<video>` or its wrapper, never both.
28: 10. Only bundled fonts (`references/format.md`) resolve by name; any other family needs `@font-face` to a file in `assets/fonts/`.
29: 11. Asset paths are root-relative (`assets/...`), in sub-compositions too.
30: 12. Grades, grain, blur, vignettes on footage go through `hyperframes media-treatment` (`media-use`), never CSS filters.
31: 13. The root is a normal document. A scene file puts its styles, markup and scripts inside `<template>` and styles its root as `#root`.
32: 14. Intended overflow/overlap: `data-layout-allow-overflow` or `data-layout-allow-overlap`.
33: 
34: ## Keep it editable
35: 
36: - One scene per sub-composition, short ids; the root holds only scene hosts, media and audio.
37: - Timed elements are written in the HTML, not made by script, each with a stable `id`.
38: - Copy, brand colors and swappable media are variables (`data-var-text`, `data-var-src`, `var(--id)`).
39: - One kind per track: `data-track-kind="graphics"` on scene and overlay hosts, `captions` on the one host that holds every caption group.
40: - Content stays in the 90% action-safe box, captions and key text in 80% title-safe. Studio draws the guides; never add them as elements.
41: 
42: ## References
43: 
44: | Read | When |
45: | --- | --- |
46: | `references/format.md` | Scenes, nesting, `data-*` attributes, variables, linked clips, layout opt-outs, lint errors |
47: | `references/runtimes.md` | GSAP facts that bite, or CSS, WAAPI, Lottie, anime.js, Three.js, canvas |
48: | `references/motion.md` | Writing any motion: timings, eases, blur, cuts, title entrances; punch-ins, speed changes, holds; stutter; seeing motion |
49: | `references/look.md` | Colors, type and style: a brand, a project `frame.md`, or one of 13 presets |
50: | `references/captions.md` | Captions: transcripts, word groups, fitting, placement |
